name: Fluid Buoyancy
description: Whether a thing floats, and how grudgingly. Buoyancy is computed from the submerged fraction against the fluid's density, so a part that is half under lifts half as hard and a heavy part sinks without needing to be told to — which is what makes a sandbox feel like it has physics rather than rules. Drag is separated from buoyancy because they are different forces that players tune for different reasons: one decides whether the boat floats, the other whether it is worth sailing. Fluid regions are volumes rather than a global water level, so a sandbox can have a bucket and a lake in the same scene.

inputs.name: fluidRegions
inputs.description: Volumes with their densities. Required: a global water level cannot express a bucket and a lake at once.

inputs.name: defaultDensity
inputs.description: Density of an unlabelled fluid, in kg/m3.

inputs.name: linearDrag
inputs.description: Resistance to movement through the fluid.

inputs.name: angularDrag
inputs.description: Resistance to rotation within the fluid.

outputs.name: submergedFraction
outputs.description: Fraction under the surface, per body.

outputs.name: floating
outputs.description: Bodies currently at rest on a surface.
